subject: Scaling & deployment follow-up: Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC — sizing clarifications
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@ledgerlabs.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & clarifying metrics from today’s discovery (Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC)

Hi Samira — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our call and a few clarifying asks so we can size a Dedicated pathway and compare it to Hosted + VPC options: 

What we heard (summary):
- Primary driver: predictable latency and cost for customer-facing inference (search / assistant flows).
- Security: strong interest in VPC/private link for auditability; on-prem not required for initial POC but might be considered later.
- Ops: Ledger Labs wants a predictable throughput baseline for SLAs and a burst headroom for Black Friday-type spikes.

Clarifying asks (to size Dedicated and tradeoffs):
1) Peak sustained TPS target (in requests/sec) for the user-facing assistant. If you target bursts, give burst TPS and duration.
2) Typical token shape: average prompt tokens and average completion tokens (or a small sample CSV).
3) Concurrency characteristics: number of concurrent long-running sessions vs short-lived calls.
4) Any hard latency SLO (p95/p99 target in ms).
5) Strict security requirements (e.g., data residency, customer-managed KMS, SOC2 evidence).
6) Preference on GPU family (if you have infra folks who prefer A10G / A100 / H100 or we should recommend).

I’ve attached a tiny CSV template (ledger-poc-tps-samples.csv) you can drop numbers into — that will let us model tokens/sec and provide a recommended Dedicated pool size + suggested GPU family and quantization profile.

Next steps I propose:
- You fill the CSV and send it back by EOD Tue (20 Apr).
- Ben and Karthik will produce a one-page sizing readout (Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC) and a proposed POC plan.
- Quick sync Wed to review the readout, then we can scope the bench run.

Thanks — happy to jump on another call to walk through the CSV if helpful.

Best,
Irene Choi
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Irene — great recap. I dropped a filled version of the CSV into the Drive link and pasted the quick answers below. Procurement is looped on this thread for timeline visibility.

Quick answers:
- Peak sustained TPS (user-facing assistant): 180 rps sustained during business hours, up to ~420 rps for ~10-15 minute bursts during events.
- Token shape (avg): prompt ~60 tokens, completion ~140 tokens (most requests are short Q&A or contextualized prompts, a small subset produce longer summaries).
- Concurrency: about 40 long-lived websocket sessions (avg 60s TTL) and many short calls (median duration 350ms).
- Latency SLO: p95 < 350ms, p99 < 800ms (user-facing).
- Security: must be VPC/private link for initial POC; we require customer-managed KMS for keys and SOC2-type evidence. Data residency is US-only.
- GPU preference: our infra team suggested A10G for cost sensitivity but they are open to A100/H100 if you recommend for latency.

Procurement note: we want a POC budget/statement of work in two weeks; target decision by end-of-May.

Let me know if you want me to export more token-profile samples from prod.

—Samira

Nice — thanks Samira for the numbers. I sketched an initial recommendation offline. High-level thoughts for the ledger workload and why Dedicated + VPC looks attractive: 

Why Dedicated + VPC is a strong fit:
- Predictable baseline: 180 rps sustained with your token shape (~200 tokens total per request) maps to ~36k tokens/sec baseline. That lines up with a modest Dedicated pool rather than pure hosted credits if you want lowest unit cost.
- Burst handling: bursts to 420 rps can be handled by burst slots + short-term autoscaling; we’ll size headroom as a % over sustained TPS for 10–15 minute events.
- Security/compliance: VPC + customer-managed KMS meets the SOC2/data residency ask and keeps logs under your control.

Preliminary Dedicated sizing (back-of-envelope):
- If we target p95 < 350ms and use an Llama-like 70B optimized runtime:
  - A single A100-40GB (well-tuned quantized runtime) can deliver roughly 8–12k tokens/sec depending on batching and prompt shape.
  - H100 or newer HBM devices will reduce latency but increase cost; they’re useful if p99 latency and low tails are a hard constraint.
  - A10G is cost-efficient for smaller models / higher multiplexing but may need more nodes for the same tail latency.

- Sizing suggestion: start with a Dedicated pool of 3 x A100-40GB slots (or 2 x H100 equivalents) as a conservative baseline:
  - Baseline throughput: ~30–36k tokens/sec (fits 180 rps x ~200 tokens).
  - Burst headroom: allow autoscale to 6 slots for 10–15 minute windows (should cover 420 rps bursts).

Operational notes and tradeoffs for the POC:
- Quantization: enable 4-bit quant profiles where quality holds; this will change GPU choice and slot counts. Karthik — can you validate model family sensitivity and recommend profiles?
- KV cache & prefix caching will cut repeated-context token work for websocket sessions; Neha, can you scope the cache config for the POC?
- Bench plan: we should run a 24-hour ramp test (sustained baseline + 2x burst simulations) with the exact token trace Samira provided. We’ll measure p95/p99 and token cost.

Next steps (owners & ETA):
- Karthik: model quantization sensitivity and GPU-family guidance — EOD Thu.
- Neha: cache and batching config for poc bench — EOD Thu.
- Irene: coordinate scheduling with Ledger for Wed review and procurement timeline.

Samira — I’ll include a one-pager that shows estimated monthly unit cost (tokens) for Hosted vs Dedicated (with reserved commit assumptions) so procurement can compare.

Thanks — Ben
